name: Dray Nur Waterfall
summary: A curtain of white water about 250 m wide on the Serepok, about 25 to 30 km south of Buon Ma Thuot. Give it a half day with the drive and come for the width of the fall, not a swim. Skip it when the coffee town is all the time you have.
getThere: About 25 km (Dak Lak culture and tourism center) or 30 km (provincial tourism handbook) south by car
heroCaption: The curtain of Dray Nur across the cliff

notice.title: The gate price changed
notice.body: A new ticket price took effect on 19 Dec 2024. Pay what the board at the gate shows, not the older 30,000 VND or 50,000 VND figures.

body: The Serepok pours over a cliff in a curtain about 250 m wide, in Krong Ana south of town. Stand on the bank in front of it first. The width is the reason to come. A walk behind the fall is allowed only where local rules permit it, and only in dry conditions.
Swim only where the staff allow it. The rock is slippery, so wear shoes that grip.
Dray Sap is the twin fall on the Dak Nong side of the river, and suspension bridges link the two about 2 km apart. Pair them when you already have a car for the day.

figures.caption: A closer stretch of the fall, with mist at the base
figures.alt: Water pouring over the Dray Nur cliff, with leaves in front and mist below

gettingThere: Dray Nur is on the Serepok in Krong Ana, about 25 to 30 km south of the city. Hire a car or join a tour from town, and make it a half day with the drive.

legs.heading: From Buon Ma Thuot
legs.body: Car or tour from the city center, about 25 to 30 km south.

admissionNote: Check on arrival. A new gate price took effect on 19 Dec 2024. Earlier figures: 30,000 VND to enter and 50,000 VND with Gia Long (Dak Lak Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism handbook), 50,000 VND (Dak Lak culture and tourism center news), and 30,000 VND as the adult scenic-site default (Dak Lak Department of Justice fee schedule).
